text.p: ING Barings Latin American Research said Tuesday it downgraded Mexican retailer Nadro SA to a hold recommendation from a buy.
Analyst Sebastian Barry-Taylor said the downgrade was due to a recent price appreciation and based on a year-end target price of $3.81.
"We forecast sales increases of 4.5 percent, 7.3 percent and 7.6 percent for 1996, 1997, and 1998 respectively," Barry-Taylor said in a report.

He said Nadro was concentrating on its core business, pharmaceutical distribution. "We estimate that the compnay is increasing market share and believe that it is positioning itself well for any possible privatization of the public sector," he added.
"Nadro has a solid balance sheet, one of the highest returns on equities of any Mexican company and a good dividend payout," it added.
